name: health
description: Liveness, readiness and startup endpoints with concurrent checks (SQLite, HTTP dependencies, files) in the application/health+json format

api.name: Status
api.sig: pub type Status = Pass | Warn | Fail derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The status of a check or of the whole service: `pass` (healthy), `warn` (healthy, with
concerns) or `fail` (unhealthy).

api.name: Value
api.sig: pub type Value = NoValue | Number{n: F64} | Count{n: Int} | Text{s: Str} | Flag{b: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: What a check measured, for `observedValue`: nothing, a number, a count, text or a flag.

api.name: Observation
api.sig: pub type Observation = {component_id: Opt[Str], component_type: Opt[Str], observed_value: Value, observed_unit: Opt[Str], status: Status, affected_endpoints: List[Str], time: Opt[Time], output: Opt[Str], links: List[(Str, Str)]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
One entry of the `checks` object: the draft's `componentId`, `componentType`, `observedValue`,
`observedUnit`, `status`, `affectedEndpoints`, `time`, `output` and `links` (relation, URI pairs).

api.name: Report
api.sig: pub type Report = {status: Status, version: Opt[Str], release_id: Opt[Str], service_id: Opt[Str], description: Opt[Str], notes: List[Str], output: Opt[Str], checks: List[(Str, List[Observation])]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A whole health response: the overall status, the service's identity and the observations keyed
by `component:measurement`, in the order the checks were given.

api.name: severity
api.sig: fn severity(s: Status) -> Int
api.doc: The severity order of statuses: pass 0, warn 1, fail 2.

api.name: worst
api.sig: fn worst(a: Status, b: Status) -> Status
api.doc: The more severe of two statuses.

api.name: status_name
api.sig: fn status_name(s: Status) -> Str
api.doc: The status's name in responses: `pass`, `warn` or `fail`.

api.name: parse_status
api.sig: fn parse_status(s: Str) -> Opt[Status]
api.doc:
Reads a status name. The draft's aliases are accepted too: `ok` and `up` for pass, `error` and
`down` for fail (any case).

api.name: http_status
api.sig: fn http_status(s: Status) -> Int
api.doc: The HTTP status for a health status: 200 for pass and warn, 503 for fail.

api.name: observation
api.sig: fn observation(s: Status, output: Str) -> Observation
api.doc: An observation with only a status (and an output for anything but pass), for custom checks.

api.name: Probe
api.sig: pub type Probe = DbPing{db: Db, query: Str} | HttpGet{url: Str, timeout_ms: Int, expect: List[Int]} | Writable{path: Str} | Exists{path: Str} | Static{obs: Observation} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
What a check does. `DbPing` runs `query` (usually `select 1`) and measures it; `HttpGet` requests
`url` within `timeout_ms` and expects a status in `expect` (any 2xx or 3xx when empty);
`Writable` creates and removes a file in the directory `path`, or appends nothing to the file
`path`; `Exists` checks that `path` exists; `Static` reports a fixed observation.

api.name: Check
api.sig: pub type Check = {name: Str where _.len > 0, measurement: Str, component_type: Str, component_id: Opt[Str], critical: Bool, warn_ms: Opt[Int], affected_endpoints: List[Str], links: List[(Str, Str)], probe: Probe} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A named check: its key in the response is `name:measurement` (just `name` when `measurement`
is empty). A check that is not `critical` makes the service `warn` instead of `fail` when it
fails (graceful degradation). With `warn_ms`, a passing check slower than that warns.

api.name: check
api.sig: fn check(name: Str where _.len > 0, p: Probe) -> Check
api.doc:
A critical check named `name` with the measurement `responseTime` and the component type
`component`.

api.name: db_check
api.sig: fn db_check(name: Str where _.len > 0, c: Db) -> Check
api.doc: A check of the database `c` with `select 1`, as the component `name` of type `datastore`.

api.name: http_check
api.sig: fn http_check(name: Str where _.len > 0, url: Str, timeout_ms: Int where _ > 0) -> Check
api.doc: A check of a dependency's URL: a GET within `timeout_ms` that must answer 2xx or 3xx.

api.name: writable_check
api.sig: fn writable_check(name: Str where _.len > 0, path: Str) -> Check
api.doc: A check that `path` (a directory, or a file) can be written, as a `system` component.

api.name: exists_check
api.sig: fn exists_check(name: Str where _.len > 0, path: Str) -> Check
api.doc: A check that `path` exists, as a `system` component.

api.name: non_critical
api.sig: fn non_critical(c: Check) -> Check
api.doc: `c` as a non-critical check: its failure makes the service warn, not fail.

api.name: check_key
api.sig: fn check_key(c: Check) -> Str
api.doc: The key of a check in the response.

api.name: run_probe
api.sig: fn run_probe(p: Probe, now: Time) -> Observation ! db, net, fs, time
api.doc: Runs one probe at `now` and gives its observation. Failures are observations, never errors.

api.name: run_check
api.sig: fn run_check(c: Check, now: Time) -> Observation ! db, net, fs, time
api.doc: Runs a check at `now`: its probe, then the check's identity, links and slowness threshold.

api.name: run_checks
api.sig: fn run_checks(cs: List[Check], now: Time) -> List[(Str, Observation)] ! db, net, fs, time, conc
api.doc:
Runs every check at once (one task each) at `now`, and gives the observations in the order of
`cs`, each with the key of its check.

api.name: contribution
api.sig: fn contribution(c: Check, o: Observation) -> Status
api.doc: The status a check contributes to the service: a failing non-critical check only warns.

api.name: group_checks
api.sig: fn group_checks(obs: List[(Str, Observation)]) -> List[(Str, List[Observation])]
api.doc: Groups keyed observations by key, keeping the first-seen order of keys.

api.name: Health
api.sig: pub type Health = {service_id: Opt[Str], version: Opt[Str], release_id: Opt[Str], description: Opt[Str], notes: List[Str], liveness: List[Check], readiness: List[Check], details: Bool, cache_ms: Int where _ >= 0, cache: Opt[Db]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A service's health setup: its identity for the response, its liveness and readiness checks,
whether responses list the checks or give the status only (`details`), and the response cache
(see `with_cache`). The started and draining state lives apart, in `Flags`.

api.name: health
api.sig: fn health(service_id: Str) -> Health
api.doc:
A health setup for the service `service_id` with no checks, details shown and no caching. Add
checks with `with readiness := [...]`.

api.name: Flags
api.sig: pub type Flags = Atomic[Int]
api.doc:
Whether the service has started and whether it is draining, shared by every handler: bit 0 is
started, bit 1 draining.

api.name: flags
api.sig: fn flags() -> Flags ! conc
api.doc: New flags: started and not draining.

api.name: with_cache
api.sig: fn with_cache(h: Health, ttl_ms: Int where _ > 0) -> Health ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
`h` with responses cached for `ttl_ms` milliseconds, in an in-memory SQLite database shared by
every handler, so a busy probe doesn't run the checks on every request.

api.name: mark_starting
api.sig: fn mark_starting(f: Flags) -> Unit ! conc
api.doc:
Marks the service as still starting: the startup and readiness endpoints fail until
`mark_started`.

api.name: mark_started
api.sig: fn mark_started(f: Flags) -> Unit ! conc
api.doc: Marks the service as started.

api.name: is_started
api.sig: fn is_started(f: Flags) -> Bool ! conc
api.doc: Whether the service has started.

api.name: start_draining
api.sig: fn start_draining(f: Flags) -> Unit ! conc
api.doc:
Starts draining: readiness fails at once (so load balancers stop sending traffic) while liveness
still passes and requests in flight finish. Call it when shutdown begins.

api.name: stop_draining
api.sig: fn stop_draining(f: Flags) -> Unit ! conc
api.doc: Stops draining.

api.name: is_draining
api.sig: fn is_draining(f: Flags) -> Bool ! conc
api.doc: Whether the service is draining.

api.name: report
api.sig: fn report(h: Health, checks: List[Check], obs: List[(Str, Observation)], extra: List[(Str, Observation)]) -> Report
api.doc: The report for `checks` with their observations and `extra` custom observations, keyed.

api.name: readiness_report
api.sig: fn readiness_report(h: Health, f: Flags, extra: List[(Str, Observation)], now: Time) -> Report ! db, net, fs, time, conc
api.doc:
Evaluates readiness at `now`: fails without running checks while starting or draining,
otherwise runs the readiness checks and folds in `extra`.

api.name: liveness_report
api.sig: fn liveness_report(h: Health, extra: List[(Str, Observation)], now: Time) -> Report ! db, net, fs, time, conc
api.doc:
Evaluates liveness at `now`: the liveness checks (often none, which passes) and `extra`.
Draining does not affect liveness, so an orchestrator doesn't restart a service that is
shutting down.

api.name: startup_report
api.sig: fn startup_report(h: Health, f: Flags) -> Report ! conc
api.doc: Evaluates startup: passes once the service is started.

api.name: json_string
api.sig: fn json_string(s: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `s` as a JSON string literal, with quotes, backslashes and control characters escaped.

api.name: to_json
api.sig: fn to_json(r: Report, details: Bool) -> Str
api.doc:
The report as `application/health+json`. With `details` false only the status (and the output of
a failure) is included, so a public endpoint doesn't reveal the service's dependencies.

api.name: respond
api.sig: fn respond(r: Report, details: Bool, method: Str) -> Response
api.doc:
The response for a report: 200 or 503, `application/health+json`, never cached by clients and
proxies, and no body for a `HEAD` request.

api.name: readiness
api.sig: fn readiness(h: Health, f: Flags, extra: List[(Str, Observation)], req: Request) -> Response ! db, net, fs, time, conc
api.doc:
The readiness endpoint: `readiness_report` with the custom observations `extra`, cached when
caching is on (the draining state is never cached: it answers at once).

api.name: liveness
api.sig: fn liveness(h: Health, extra: List[(Str, Observation)], req: Request) -> Response ! db, net, fs, time, conc
api.doc: The liveness endpoint, cached when caching is on.

api.name: startup
api.sig: fn startup(h: Health, f: Flags, req: Request) -> Response ! conc
api.doc: The startup endpoint.

api.name: Paths
api.sig: pub type Paths = {live: Str, ready: Str, startup: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: The paths the endpoints answer on.

api.name: default_paths
api.sig: fn default_paths() -> Paths
api.doc: `/health/live`, `/health/ready` and `/health/startup`.

api.name: routes
api.sig: fn routes[e](h: Health, f: Flags, p: Paths, req: Request, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Response ! db, net, fs, time, conc, e
api.doc:
Answers `GET` and `HEAD` requests for the three paths and passes everything else to `next`,
so it goes in front of a handler: `req => health.routes(h, f, health.default_paths(), req, api)`.
Other methods on a health path get 405 with `Allow`.
